blocks.content: 1. INTRODUCTION TO ADJECTIVES

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Mastery over the order and position of adjectives is crucial for competitive grammar sections.
High-probability exam topics include irregular adjective forms and common comparative structures.
Critical distinction rules apply to subtle pairs such as Few vs A Few, Little vs A Little, Less vs Fewer, and Elder vs Older.
Key sentence structures like As...As, So...That, Too...To, and Enough frequently form the basis of error-spotting questions.

blocks.content:
An adjective is a word that describes, qualifies, or modifies a noun or pronoun.

It provides additional information about size, shape, color, quantity, number, quality, and possession.



Examples:

• a tall building

• three students

• a happy child



Adjectives are extremely important for SSC examinations because they are frequently tested in:

• Error Detection

• Sentence Improvement

• Fill in the Blanks

• Cloze Tests



Golden Principle:

An adjective always adds meaning to a noun — never stands alone.
2. TYPES OF ADJECTIVES

Understanding types of adjectives is essential for grammatical accuracy.



Major Types:



1. Adjectives of Quality – describe nature or characteristics.

Example: a beautiful painting



2. Adjectives of Quantity – indicate amount.

Example: some water



3. Adjectives of Number – indicate count.

Example: five books



4. Demonstrative Adjectives – point out nouns.

Example: this book, those students



5. Possessive Adjectives – show ownership.

Example: my car, her bag



6. Interrogative Adjectives – used in questions.

Example: which pen? whose book?



7. Distributive Adjectives – refer to members individually.

Example: each student, every child
3. POSITION OF ADJECTIVES

Adjectives are generally placed in two positions:



1. Before the noun:

• She bought a red dress.



2. After linking verbs (is, am, are, seem, become):

• The sky is blue.



IMPORTANT RULE:

Do not use an adjective when an adverb is required.



Incorrect: She sings beautiful.

Correct: She sings beautifully.
4. ORDER OF ADJECTIVES (VERY IMPORTANT FOR SSC)

When multiple adjectives describe a noun, they must follow a specific order:



Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Color → Origin → Material → Purpose → Noun



Example:

• a beautiful small old round red Italian wooden table



Memory Trick:

OSASCOMP (Opinion, Size, Age, Shape, Color, Origin, Material, Purpose)
5. COMPARISON OF ADJECTIVES

Adjectives have three degrees:



1. Positive Degree – no comparison.

Example: tall



2. Comparative Degree – compares two.

Example: taller



3. Superlative Degree – compares more than two.

Example: tallest
6. FORMATION RULES FOR COMPARISON

Short Adjectives:

Add 'er' and 'est'.

• fast → faster → fastest



Adjectives ending in 'y':

Change y to i.

• happy → happier → happiest



Long Adjectives:

Use more / most.

• beautiful → more beautiful → most beautiful
7. IRREGULAR ADJECTIVES (HIGH-PROBABILITY SSC)

good → better → best

bad → worse → worst

little → less → least

many/much → more → most

far → farther/further → farthest/furthest
8. IMPORTANT RULES OF COMPARISON

Rule 1:

Use 'than' with comparative degree.

Incorrect: She is taller to me.

Correct: She is taller than me.



Rule 2:

Use 'the' before superlative.

• the tallest building



Rule 3:

Do not use double comparison.

Incorrect: more better

Correct: better
9. VERY IMPORTANT SSC STRUCTURES

• No other + singular noun + is as + positive + as

Example:

No other city is as crowded as Mumbai.



• One of the + superlative + plural noun

Example:

She is one of the best players.



• Prefer X to Y (NOT than)

Correct: I prefer tea to coffee.
10. AS…AS STRUCTURE

Used for equal comparison.



• She is as tall as her sister.



Negative:

• She is not as tall as her sister.
11. SO…THAT STRUCTURE

Used to show result.



• He was so tired that he fell asleep.
12. TOO…TO STRUCTURE

Indicates impossibility.



• The box is too heavy to lift.
13. ENOUGH STRUCTURE

Adjective + enough + to + verb



• She is smart enough to solve it.

rows: FEW vs A FEW / LITTLE vs A LITTLE
Non-countable degree/amount vs. Countable plural items
Time sequence vs. Order of position
Family relations/members vs. General age comparison
Uncountable nouns vs. Plural countable nouns

blocks.content: 14. FEW vs A FEW / LITTLE vs A LITTLE (SSC FAVORITE)

Few → almost none (negative meaning)

A few → some (positive meaning)



Little → hardly any

A little → some



Example:

• Few students passed. (almost none)

• A few students passed. (some)
15. LESS vs FEWER

Fewer → used with countable nouns.

• fewer students



Less → used with uncountable nouns.

• less water
16. LATER vs LATTER / ELDER vs OLDER

Later → time

Latter → second of two



Elder → used for family members

Older → used generally
17. MUCH vs MANY vs A LOT OF

Many → countable nouns

Much → uncountable nouns

A lot of → both
18. MOST vs MOST OF

Most → general meaning

• Most people agree.



Most of → specific group

• Most of the students passed.
19. ADJECTIVES THAT LOOK LIKE ADVERBS

Some words function as both adjective and adverb.



• fast

• late

• early



Example:

• a fast train (adjective)

• run fast (adverb)

items: FEW vs A FEW / LITTLE vs A LITTLE is marked as an SSC Favorite for error detection questions.
The exact sequence in 'ORDER OF ADJECTIVES' is tested extensively in sentence improvement and spotting errors.
Pay special attention to 'IRREGULAR ADJECTIVES' and adjectives that look like adverbs, as these are high-probability exam topics.

blocks.content: 20. HIGH-PROBABILITY SSC RULES

1. Never use double comparatives.

2. Use 'than' with comparative.

3. Always use 'the' before superlative.

4. Learn irregular forms.

5. Follow correct adjective order.

6. Understand few/little differences.
21. COMMON ERRORS IN EXAMINATIONS

Incorrect: She is more smarter than me.

Correct: She is smarter than me.



Incorrect: He is the most tallest boy.

Correct: He is the tallest boy.



Incorrect: There are less students today.

Correct: There are fewer students today.
22. PRACTICE QUESTIONS (SSC LEVEL)

Fill in the blanks:



1. She is ______ than her brother. (tall/taller)

2. This is the ______ building in the city. (high/highest)

3. ______ students attended the lecture. (few/a few)

4. I prefer coffee ___ tea.



Error Detection:



1. He is more better now.

2. She is senior than me.

3. This is one of the best player.



Answers:

taller, highest, a few, to



Errors:

remove 'more', than → to, player → players
23. CHAPTER SUMMARY

Adjectives enhance sentence clarity by describing nouns precisely.



Key Takeaways:



• Learn adjective order.

• Master comparison rules.

• Avoid double comparison.

• Understand few/little usage.

• Remember irregular forms.
